Below is the most extended list of Venus transits to be published up to date
(October 6, 2003), thanks to Solex 8.5!
The list contains the 2544 Venus transits taking place between 100,000 BC and
100,000 AD, sorted in descending order.

The Date and Time are given for the point of minimum angular distance.
Lines marked with an asterisk indicate transits occurring very close to the
border of the solar disk, within the uncertainty limit for the given epoch.

Dm = minimum geocentric apparent angle, in degrees.
Dl = limiting angle to observe a transit.
p  =  position angle, relative to the center of the solar disk, of the point
      of minimum angular distance, measured clockwise from South=0.
RA and Decl (degrees) are referred to the equator and equinox of J2000.

Please note that the time is expressed as Dynamical (or Ephemeris) Time, not
as UT. Also, dates before AD 1600 are in the Julian Calendar, those
after AD 1600 are in the ordinary (unmodified) Gregorian calendar.

lines below are compared for the year 49958:

    solar system, including Ceres, Pallas and Vesta;

    arithmetics)
